title: Bind the exact registered backend before comparing operator signatures
applies_when: A custom-op, fake/meta, sharding or backend-forwarding allegation compares similar names or a Python alias that resolves differently across platforms.
lesson: Resolve the complete operator name and platform-dependent binding, then read that exact schema and implementation. Similar prefixes or Python aliases do not establish identity. In TorchAO, custom_sharding_for_cutedsl_mxfp8_2d_1x32_kernel registers mxfp8_quantize_2d_1x32_cutedsl with two outputs, not the neighboring four-output mxfp8_quantize_2d_1x32_32x1_cutedsl. In SGLang, the CPU AMX flash_attn_varlen_func alias resolves to torch.ops.sgl_kernel, while XPU imports a different implementation under the same name. The cited CPU schema has no softmax_scale argument and its C++ implementation computes 1/sqrt(head_size). Merely forwarding the keyword, with a permissive mock accepting it, cannot qualify a native fix. The cited Gemma4 model already avoids AMX by default for scale/mask limitations. First inspect the real consumer and supported caller reachability; then decide whether a native API change, a compatible fallback, or no change is appropriate.
avoid_when: Each case is a source-only counterexample to a particular arity claim or a Python-only forwarding repair, not execution of TorchAO, DTensor, CuTe DSL or AMX attention. The SGLang scale limitation is real in the cited source; this lesson does not prove every model is protected, an explicit AMX override is safe, or a supported failing caller is absent. A schema/implementation mismatch can still be a bug. Mocked forwarding tests can isolate wrapper behavior but do not validate an actual backend schema or numerical result. No measured Scout accuracy, cost or PR-conversion improvement is established.

evidence.note: Decorator names the non-fused 1x32 operator; each declared sharding has two output placements. Static binding evidence only.
The registered non-fused implementation returns qdata and scales. The adjacent fused 1x32_32x1 operator is a distinct four-output entry, not this sharding rule's target.

CPU AMX binds the Python name to torch.ops.sgl_kernel; XPU imports its own flash_attn implementation. AMX ignores softmax_scale supplied by the common caller, while XPU forwards it. This source comparison alone is not native qualification.
The registered CPU flash_attn_varlen_func schema accepts q/k/v, cumulative sequence lengths, maximum lengths and causal, but no scale keyword.
The exact CPU implementation computes sm_scale from head_size internally. No native numerical test or proposed API change was executed for this observation.

Gemma4 selects SDPA by default on CPU and explicitly documents AMX scale/mask limitations; an explicit user backend override remains separate. This is a caller-specific protection, not a universal absence-of-bug claim.
